problem: If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=4$ and $f(4)=2,$ then what is ${lim}_{x\to 4}{({x}^{2}-6f(x))}^{2}?$

feedback.problem: If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=-1$ and ${lim}_{x\to {(-1)}^{-}}f(x)=8,$ then what is the value of $\sqrt{f(-1)+1}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We're told that $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=-1.$ According to the definition of continuity, this means that ${lim}_{x\to (-1)}f(x)$ exists, and

$$
f(-1)={lim}_{x\to {(-1)}^{-}}f(x)=8.
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{f(-1)+1} & =\sqrt{8+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
